rows.title: The Sylow Theorems: Existence, Conjugacy and Counting

sections.heading: Introduction and notation
sections.body: The Sylow theorems are the first structural results about finite groups beyond Lagrange's theorem. We give self-contained proofs of existence (Sylow I), conjugacy (Sylow II) and the counting conditions (Sylow III), together with the index formula for the normalizer and the uniqueness criterion. Notation is fixed in Section 2; all results are stated and proved in Section 3; examples and references follow.

sections.heading: Definitions and notation
sections.body: |G| order; p-Sylow subgroup = subgroup of order p^k where p^k is the full p-part of |G|; N_G(H) normalizer; orbit-stabilizer; class equation; fixed-point congruence for p-groups.

sections.heading: Main results
sections.body: Theorem 3.1 (Sylow I): existence and containment. Theorem 3.2 (Sylow II): conjugacy. Theorem 3.3 (Sylow III): n_p | m and n_p = 1 (mod p). Theorem 3.4: n_p = [G : N_G(P)]. Theorem 3.5: uniqueness iff normality.

sections.heading: Examples and comparison with the literature
sections.body: S_3, S_4, A_5 and groups of order pq illustrate the counting conditions; the treatment follows the expository accounts of the reference list.

claims.text: Let G be a finite group and p a prime with |G| = p^k m, where p does not divide m. Then G contains a Sylow p-subgroup of order p^k, and every p-subgroup of G is contained in some Sylow p-subgroup of G.
claims.disclaimer: 数值交叉验证，不构成证明

claims.text: Any two Sylow p-subgroups of a finite group G are conjugate: if H and K both have order p^k then K = gHg^{-1} for some g in G.
claims.disclaimer: 数值交叉验证，不构成证明

claims.text: Let |G| = p^k m with p not dividing m and let n_p be the number of Sylow p-subgroups of G. Then n_p divides m and n_p is congruent to 1 modulo p.
claims.disclaimer: 数值交叉验证，不构成证明

claims.text: For every Sylow p-subgroup P of a finite group G, the number of Sylow p-subgroups equals the index of the normalizer, n_p = [G : N_G(P)].
claims.disclaimer: 数值交叉验证，不构成证明

claims.text: A Sylow p-subgroup P of a finite group G is the unique Sylow p-subgroup if and only if P is normal in G; in particular, if G is abelian then each of its Sylow subgroups is unique.
claims.disclaimer: 数值交叉验证，不构成证明
